text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Police have arrested 14 members of a crime ring charged with the killing of the general director of prisons and a bomb attack that killed four. They could face capital punishment.
- The son-in-law of late Albanian dictator Enver Hoxha, Klement Kolaneci, has been arrested on charges of heading a criminal band and faces a maximum penalty of life in jail.

- Europe's elections watchdog, a branch of the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe, has withdrawn from monitoring local polls in Albania on Sunday after the government approved less than half its list of observers.

- Foreign Minister Tritan Shehu says a climate of mistrust exists between Albania's government and OSCE because its report on May's general elections did not correspond with other reports by international observers and was the most negative.

- Opposition parties say the government's refusal to allow the OSCE's mission to monitor Albanian polls is a primitive act of revenge against the OSCE for the objective report it issued on the country's disputed general polls in May.
- President Sali Berisha on Wednesday turned down a call by five opposition parties to cut voting times in Sunday's municipal elections by three hours.
- Albania is Europe's poorest country and its people spend two thirds of their income on food and tobacco.
- An Albanian appeals court upheld a previous ruling sentencing a Briton to two years jail for sexually abusing two minors.
- Members of a guerrilla group have confessed to killing the general director of prisons Bujar Kaloshi and to planting a bomb that killed four.
- The key opposition Socialist Party says it has discovered 7,100 irregularities in voters lists in 102 polling stations.
- Former Austrian Foreign Minister Alois Mock praises Albania's foreign policy as contributing to stability in the Balkan region.
